scope: Five selected studies; abstract-level evidence; not a complete or current treatment review
generation_method: Assistant-authored reference, checked against curated evidence

claims.text: Certain LRRK2 mutations segregated with inherited parkinsonism in families.
G2019S was present in 8 of 482 patients in this study of idiopathic Parkinson’s disease.
Pathogenic LRRK2 variants increased Rab protein phosphorylation in laboratory experiments.
This study estimated Parkinson’s risk in G2019S carriers at 28% by age 59, 51% by 69, and 74% by 79.
The reported G2019S risk estimates remain below 100% through the ages studied; carrying the mutation does not guarantee disease by those ages.
DNL201 inhibited LRRK2 and was well tolerated at doses demonstrating pathway engagement in phase 1 and 1b trials.
The DNL201 target-inhibition and tolerability finding does not establish that the drug slows Parkinson’s.

research_questions.question: Does inhibiting LRRK2 slow Parkinson’s progression?
Which patients might benefit, with or without particular LRRK2 mutations?
Does changing Rab phosphorylation improve disease outcomes?
